answer: Lineage-exclusive seats (proposal): each credential fixes a lineage id; a seat stays live only after its epoch update signed with that key. The chain takes the first update per lineage — a second signature from any copy is proof of cloning and burns the seat. Copying the plans of a wharf adds cranes, not berths: clones crowd one ledge, first stands, second burns the seat, so a farm of copies holds one knoll, not a range. Copies buy redundancy, not capacity. Buying N credentials yields N seats — linear, profit only if each price sits under its seat's rewards; bulk issuance remains the seam.
